reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) discusses thermal stability and grain growth in HEAs, Mn-based redox buffering in molten salts, and recrystallization/coarsening in an HEA, but none provides specific support for the key premises about grain-boundary-mediated diffusion of oxygen/salt species in Q235 steel, the effect of grain size on oxide uniformity/spallation, or the negligible room-temperature effect. The premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Grain boundaries act as fast-diffusion pathways for oxygen and salt species at 700–900 °C
Finer grain structure accelerates diffusion and leads to non-uniform oxide and spallation
Coarser grain structure restricts diffusion and promotes uniform, adherent protective oxide
At room temperature, diffusional kinetics are too slow for grain size to affect corrosion
Annealing can control grain size in Q235 steel without altering composition
